standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the reduction to the case x, y in A and the final evaluation of the two symbols modulo the maximal ideal.

core_obligations: Reduce by multiplicativity of d_A to the case where x and y lie in A, and write x = t^a u, y = t^b v with t a uniformizer and u, v units (proof lines 17637-17640).

With l = a + b, verify that t^{l-1}, ..., t^b is an admissible sequence in (x)/(xy) and t^{l-1}, ..., t^a is an admissible sequence in (y)/(xy), and use the characterisation of the symbol to write down the equation computing d_A(x, y) with the sign (-1)^{ab} (proof lines 17640-17650).
Evaluate the two displayed symbols through the admissible relations to obtain d_A(x, y) = (-1)^{ab} u^a / v^b modulo m_A, which is the usual tame symbol (proof lines 17651-17656).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to x, y in A and introduce the uniformizer and the unit parts (proof lines 17637-17640).
Choose the two admissible sequences and apply the characterisation of the symbol with the sign (-1)^{ab} (proof lines 17640-17650).
Evaluate through the admissible relations to reach the usual tame symbol (proof lines 17651-17656).
difficulty_reason: For a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K and nonzero x, y in K, the lemma identifies the symbol d_A(x, y) with (-1)^{ord_A(x) ord_A(y)} x^{ord_A(y)} / y^{ord_A(x)} modulo the maximal ideal (statement lines 17623-17634). The proof first uses multiplicativity of the symbol to reduce to x, y in A, writes x = t^a u and y = t^b v with t a uniformizer and u, v units, sets l = a + b, observes that t^{l-1}, ..., t^b is an admissible sequence in (x)/(xy) and t^{l-1}, ..., t^a is an admissible sequence in (y)/(xy), and invokes the characterisation of the symbol by a single comparison of two such symbols to obtain the equation defining d_A(x, y) with the sign (-1)^{ab} (proof lines 17637-17650). The last step evaluates the two symbols through the admissible relations to get d_A(x, y) = (-1)^{ab} u^a / v^b mod m_A (proof lines 17651-17654). Choosing the two admissible sequences in the quotients correctly and reducing the comparison to the unit parts is the non-formal content, so the claim is H2.
